subject: Usage smoothing: unit-econ recap, burst guardrails & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Usage smoothing: unit-econ recap, burst guardrails & next steps

Hi Samira — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so your procurement and engineering teams have something to react to.

Summary of your expected shape (from call):
- Typical steady usage: ~200k tokens/day (~6M tokens/month)
- Weekly peak test windows: 10–20M tokens over 2–4 hour windows (approx 1.5–2.5x typical qps)
- Initial pilot budget target: $3k–$6k/month (editable if we shift commitment)
- Success metric for pilot: <200ms median latency, no throttling during scheduled test windows, <10% overage spend relative to committed band

Proposed commercial and ops starting points (attached unit econ spreadsheet):
- Target list price: $980 per 1M tokens for gen endpoints (pilot tier pricing shown in sheet).
- Recommended committed band: 5M tokens/month with a soft quota + burst allowance.
- Soft quota behavior: soft cap at committed band; requests beyond are accepted within burst window for up to 48 hours with no immediate enforced hard block.
- Burst guardrail: rolling 4-hour burst window capped at 3x your steady qps; above that triggers throttling or routed to a lower-cost variant (we can auto-fallback).
- Overage pricing: $1,400 / 1M tokens for sustained usage >120% of committed band for the monthly bill period. Overage credit: we typically offer a 100% credit on the first-month overage for pilots (one-time; Marissa can confirm).

Action items for you:
1) Confirm monthly budget target (pick a band from the sheet) — Samira/Procurement.
2) Share expected scheduled test windows (UTC ranges) and peak QPS numbers for engineering to validate latency SLOs.
3) Procurement: let us know if Acuity needs different wording on soft quota / overage caps — we can produce a redline-friendly addendum.

I'll leave Marissa on copy for the formal pilot SOW and Neha on the technical routing/quotas. If this looks right I'll send a short one-page pilot SOW + a proposed SLA addendum for burst behavior.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment(s): redwood_unit_econ_1M_v2.xlsx

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@acuityhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acuityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Usage smoothing: unit-econ recap, burst guardrails & next steps

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after showing this to engineering and procurement: 

1) Numbers — we're leaning toward a pilot at the $4k/month mid-band. That aligns with the 5M committed band you suggested.
2) Peak windows — our regular load tests are Tuesdays 17:00–21:00 UTC and one end-to-end system test on the 3rd Wednesday of the month, usually a 3-hour window where qps jumps ~2.2x. We can provide exact traces if needed.
3) Burst behavior — procurement's request: can we get a written limit on the rolling burst (e.g., 4-hour cap at 3x steady qps) plus an explicit overage cap for pilot at 150% of committed band (after which calls are throttled) instead of open-ended overage billing? They want predictability.
4) Security/POC notes — we will need an SOC2 evidence checklist and a 30-day log retention confirmation for the pilot (forwarding to our security team separately).

Also, is there any chance Redwood can credit the first pilot month overage beyond the single-credit you mentioned? Our first run historically spikes because data ingest and warm caches push tokens up. If you can do 2x first-month overage credit (or a one-time $2k credit), that helps us get the exec sign-off.

If that works I'll loop in procurement formally and they can route a SOW or DocuSign for the pilot.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Platform | Acuity Health
samira.k@acuityhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-09-16T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Usage smoothing: unit-econ recap, burst guardrails & next steps

Hi Samira — thanks for the quick turnaround and for raising procurement's preference for predictability. A few commitments and options so procurement has language to work with: 

Commercial commitments for the pilot (proposal):
- Pilot price band: $4,000/month (5M committed tokens).
- Soft quota + burst: Rolling 4-hour window capped at 3x steady qps for accepted bursts.
- Pilot hard throttle cap: 150% of committed band for pilot month. Once sustained >150% we will throttle to protect other tenants.
- Overage pricing beyond the 150% hard throttle (if customer requests raising to a higher committed band mid-month): $1,200 / 1M tokens (discounted pilot rate) applied prospectively.
- First-month concession: Redwood will apply a one-time credit covering up to 100% of the first-month overage (i.e., we will waive first-month overages up to the equivalent of 100% of committed band). We cannot extend 2x overage credits as a standard, but can consider a $2k marketing credit on top of the first-month overage waiver for pilot customers that sign within 10 business days — Marissa can confirm approval.

Operational notes for engineering (Neha):
- We'll provision a soft quota with automatic telemetry alerts at 80/100/120% of committed band and a routing policy that will attempt an auto-fallback to a lower-cost gen variant when throttling is imminent.
- For scheduled test windows you can request a temporary bump (48-hour scheduled burst) by emailing support@redwood.ai with at least 24-hour notice; auto-approval for pilot customers up to +2x steady qps.

Next steps: 
1) Samira/procurement to confirm pilot budget ($4k/month) and accept the pilot hard throttle at 150% for month one.
2) If accepted, Marissa will send the one-page SOW + SLA addendum and a DocuSign link for signatures.
3) Neha will send a short checklist for engineering traces we need to validate latency SLOs.

Marissa — can you confirm the marketing credit flow and get final sign-off on the one-time $2k credit if procurement pushes for it?

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): acuity_pilot_ma_plan.pdf

Ben / Samira — quick note from the commercial approvals side: 

- Confirmed: Redwood can offer the one-time $2,000 marketing credit in addition to the first-month overage waiver for pilots that sign the SOW within 10 business days of the SOW issue date.
- We'll include explicit language in Section 3.2 of the SOW: "Pilot overage waiver: Redwood will waive billable overages up to 100% of the committed band for the first month of the pilot. Any usage beyond 150% of the committed band will be subject to throttling. A one-time marketing credit of $2,000 will be applied to the first invoice upon execution, provided the SOW is signed within 10 business days."

Samira — if that works for Acuity, I will prepare the DocuSign package and get it over. Neha, please attach the engineering checklist with traces when you send the pilot onboarding email.
